blocks.prompt: 16. If the \(p^{\text{th}}\) term of an A.P. is \(q\) and the \(q^{\text{th}}\) term is \(p\), prove that its \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is \((p + q - n)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof hai, lekin numbers ki jagah letters hain. Idea bilkul sawal 10 wala hai: do terms maloom hon to \(a_1\) aur \(d\) nikal aate hain.
Saabit kya karna hai? \(n\)th term \(p + q - n\) hai.
Plan: do equations, minus kar ke \(d\), phir \(a_1\), aur aakhir mein \(a_n\) mein rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_p = q,\ a_q = p\) (aur \(p \ne q\))
Saabit karna hai: \(a_n = p + q - n\).
Tareeqa: General term \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\). Letters se ghabrayein nahi; inhein numbers ki tarah hi treat karein.

Do equations likhein
\[a_1 + (p - 1)d = q \quad (1)\]
\[a_1 + (q - 1)d = p \quad (2)\]
Kyun: General term mein pehle \(n = p\), phir \(n = q\) rakha. \(p\)th term \(q\) hai aur \(q\)th term \(p\) hai.

Minus kar ke \(d\) nikalein
\[(1) - (2):\ (p - q)d = q - p\]
\[d = \dfrac{q - p}{p - q} = -1\]
Kyun: \(a_1\) cancel ho gaya. \(d\) ke coefficients: \((p - 1) - (q - 1) = p - q\). Right side: \(q - p\). \(p \ne q\) hai, is liye \(p - q\) se divide kar sakte hain. \(q - p\) aur \(p - q\) ek doosre ke negative hain, is liye \(d = -1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{q - p}{p - q}\) ko 1 samajh lena aam ghalti hai; yeh hamesha \(-1\) hota hai.

\(a_1\) nikalein
\[a_1 + (p - 1)(-1) = q\]
\[a_1 = p + q - 1\]
Kyun: \(d = -1\) ko (1) mein rakha: \(a_1 - p + 1 = q\). Phir \(-p + 1\) ko doosri taraf le gaye.

\(a_n\) nikalein
\[a_n = (p + q - 1) + (n - 1)(-1)\]
\[= p + q - 1 - n + 1\]
\[= p + q - n\]
Kyun: \(a_1\) aur \(d\) dono general term mein rakhe. \((n - 1)(-1) = -n + 1\); phir \(-1\) aur \(+1\) cancel ho gaye.

Tasdeeq
\[a_p = p + q - p = q \;\checkmark\]
\[a_q = p + q - q = p \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Hamare formula mein \(n = p\) aur \(n = q\) rakha to dono di hui baatein wapas mil gayin.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(n\)th term \(p + q - n\) hai.
